pending_interview.category: System design (general) — scalability patterns; designing common systems like a URL shortener, rate limiter, chat system, notification system
pending_interview.question: You are designing a notification delivery system for a large consumer platform. The system needs to send notifications across multiple channels — push, SMS, and email — to hundreds of millions of users. Notifications vary widely in urgency: some are time-critical (like a one-time login code), others are low-priority (like a weekly digest). Walk through your high-level architecture. How do you ensure high-priority messages are never delayed by a backlog of low-priority ones? How do you handle retries when a downstream channel (e.g., an SMS provider) is temporarily down? And how does the system scale to handle a sudden spike — say, a major platform event that triggers notifications to 50 million users within 60 seconds?
